why: Round 2 (shape+rf) scored 0.82 on unseen bearings but about 0.51 when trained at one load and tested at another. A drive knows its load setting and how its other motors sound at that load, without knowing which are damaged. Round 3 compares each recording with the fleet at the same condition, so a load change should cancel out.
fleet_normal: for each condition and each feature: (x - median) / (IQR + 1e-6), median and IQR over the usable recordings of the reference bearings at that condition, without labels. Reference bearings = the training bearings of the fold (inner folds: the inner training bearings). Setting columns stay raw.
own_normal: each recording's band levels minus that recording's mean band level
model: RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=300, min_samples_leaf=10, max_features='sqrt', class_weight='balanced_subsample', random_state=0), as round 2
same_load_test: as round 2: round-1 folds, all four conditions mixed, inner out-of-fold scores on the 5 training groups set the calibration, line and band; one outer pass
new_load_test: for N15_M07_F10 -> N15_M01_F10 and the reverse: labels from training bearings at the training load only; the fleet normal at the test load uses training bearings' recordings at the test load without labels; calibration, line and band from inner out-of-fold scores at the training load; test bearings at the test load scored once
seen_bearings_number: the same detector with recordings split at random (5 folds, seed 0), fleet normal from all bearings, reported as inflated
plant_switch: the plant view uses round 3 at 16k_12b only if the lower end of the 95% range is above 0.5 for the same-load test AND for both new-load directions at 16k_12b; otherwise it stays on round 2

ring_fr003.task: outer ring (KA*) vs inner ring (KI*), damaged bearings only; KB23 KB24 KB27 (both rings, Lessmeier Table 5) never used to train or score
ring_fr003.features: all_fleet (band_, contrast_, click_ with the fleet normal)
ring_fr003.test: same outer folds; trained on the fold's KA/KI training bearings; scored per recording as balanced accuracy outer vs inner; 95% range by resampling bearings
ring_fr003.show_rule: the product names a ring only if, at 16k_12b, the lower end of the ring score's 95% range is above 0.5; then a check-bearing motor shows 'outer ring likely' if its median outer-ring estimate is 0.65 or more, 'inner ring likely' if 0.35 or less, else 'cannot tell'. If the rule fails, every motor shows 'which ring: cannot tell'.

damage_size_fr014: from the round-3 same-load predictions at lab and 16k_12b: share of recordings flagged per damage level (Lessmeier Tables 4 and 5: level 1 = 15 bearings, level 2 = 9, level 3 = 2), with bearing counts; and per motor in the plant view

authors_split_fr020.task: 3 classes, same forest, all four conditions, fleet normal from the training bearings only
authors_split_fr020.metrics: plain accuracy per recording (their Table 9 metric) and balanced 3-class accuracy; both feature sets reported, none chosen
authors_split_fr020.compare_with: Lessmeier 2016 Table 9, motor current: 26.8% to 60.9%, ensemble 45.9%; guessing 33.3%

reported: all three rounds; every candidate's own score at every setting; round 1 stays the result sealed first
